Insurrection

in-suh-REK-shun -- shares a root with 'resurrect,' meaning to rise. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Insurrection is a violent uprising against an established authority.

Soldiers were called in overnight after an armed insurrection broke out near the capitol steps.

Worked Example

A group of angry factory workers seizes control of the building overnight, blocking every entrance and demanding the owner be removed by force.

That organized, violent rising-up against authority is exactly what an insurrection is. Unlike 'protest,' which can be entirely peaceful, insurrection specifically implies force and open rebellion.

How Insurrection Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

rebellion

rebellion: organized resistance against authority

revolt

revolt: a violent uprising against a government or ruler

uprising

uprising: an act of resistance or rebellion

Antonyms

compliance

compliance: obedience to rules or authority

submission

submission: the act of yielding to another's authority

How Strong Is It? — uprising → insurrection → revolt

uprising vs. insurrection

uprising vs. insurrection: Uprising is a slightly more general word than insurrection -- an uprising can describe any large-scale resistance, while insurrection often implies a more organized, armed attempt to seize power.

revolt vs. insurrection

revolt vs. insurrection: Revolt can feel similar in force to insurrection, though insurrection specifically emphasizes rising up against an established authority, while revolt can also describe smaller acts of open defiance.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — in-

Prefix — in-: against, upon (Latin)

Root — surrect

Root — surrect: to rise (from Latin surgere, 'to rise'; surrectus is its past form, as in resurrect)

Suffix — -ion

Suffix — -ion: act or process of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: In- ('against, upon') + surrect ('to rise' — from Latin surgere, whose past form surrectus appears in resurrect) + -ion ('act or process of'): Latin insurgere meant 'to rise up against.' An insurrection, at its root, is a rising-up against authority — the same root that gives us resurrect and surge.

Use the root in a new word: resurrect

Use the root in a new word: resurrect: The old bakery on Main Street was resurrected by a new owner who kept every original recipe.
